title: India's Defence UAV Start-ups Are Crossing From Prototype to Delivery
excerpt: Private Indian UAV makers are now visible at the delivery and DPSU-partnership stage, not only the demonstration stage — but the evidence stops at the platform and says nothing about what is inside it.

body.text: Private Indian UAV makers are now visible at the delivery and DPSU-partnership stage, not only the demonstration stage — but the evidence stops at the platform and says nothing about what is inside it.

items: Drogo Aerospace: first batch of 41 JK 250e drones reported delivered to Army Southern Command (Nashik) in June 2026 under a ₹72 crore contract (L2, multiple outlets; no MoD primary).
Drogo Aerospace – Munitions India Ltd MoU (4 Sep 2026) for indigenous UAVs and loitering munitions (L2). An MoU is not an order.
VU Dynamics (IIT Kanpur SIIC) partnership with PATH Group; BusinessLine reports a takeover and an Indore factory (L2).
Delivery evidence shifts the question from "can they build it" to "what is in the bill of materials".
DPSU partnerships give private designers a production and qualification route for loitering munitions.
No MoD primary contract document located for the JK 250e order.
VU Dynamics ownership (takeover vs collaboration) unresolved.
Subsystem origin for every platform undisclosed.

title: The Hidden Semiconductor Dependency of Indian UAVs
excerpt: Indian drone avionics are increasingly designed in India, but the silicon inside them arrives through distributors' drone portfolios — which makes distributors the clearest window onto the dependency.

body.text: Indian drone avionics are increasingly designed in India, but the silicon inside them arrives through distributors' drone portfolios — which makes distributors the clearest window onto the dependency.

items: Millennium Semiconductors publishes a drone component portfolio spanning processors, CMOS sensors, GNSS/cellular, motor control, MOSFETs, Hall sensors, BMS and power — from globally sourced brands (L3).
Indian flight-controller vendors (Arkin Labs, YARI Robotics, Zerosum) claim Indian design but disclose no semiconductor BOM (L3).
Techadyant UAS sovereignty table already scores MCU/SoC, IMU, PMIC and power electronics among the highest-risk layers (internal, indicative).
"Designed in India" at board level and "dependent on imports" at chip level are both true at once.
Distributor line cards are a repeatable, low-cost dependency-tracking method.
Specific brands in the portfolio were not re-verified in this pass.
No Indian FC vendor BOM is public.

title: India's Drone Battery Question Is Really a Cell Question
excerpt: Drone Expo 2026 showed Indian pack and BMS integration — including semi-solid-state packs — but not one verified Indian drone-cell source. Pack localisation is being mistaken for battery localisation.

body.text: Drone Expo 2026 showed Indian pack and BMS integration — including semi-solid-state packs — but not one verified Indian drone-cell source. Pack localisation is being mistaken for battery localisation.

items: Ascend Powerpacks claims in-house design and manufacture of drone packs, BMS and chargers; cell origin undisclosed (L3).
Six further energy exhibitors (Nsure, Godi Nova, Enovix R&D India, ATC Energies, FC TecNrgy, XINGTO) — none with verified drone-cell manufacturing (L5).
Existing Atlas: "cells are the imported core of domestically assembled packs".
Endurance and payload — the performance levers defence buyers care about — are set by a cell India does not yet evidently make for drones.
Pack makers are the natural first customers for any Indian drone-grade cell line.
